memory_update.text: CAMT should remain a high-priority Layer 2 candidate for HBM/advanced-packaging inspection because the gathered evidence includes explicit 2026 orders from a leading HBM manufacturer and tier-1 OSAT for AI-related applications.

FORM is a strong second-order probe-card candidate: its product evidence explicitly links HFTAP probe cards to HBM stack devices, fine-pitch interposers, known-good-die memory testing, and advanced packaging.
KLIC belongs in the advanced bonding subnode. Evidence supports HBM-adjacent memory bonding exposure, but production qualification with top HBM makers still needs verification.
ACMR is a speculative shadow candidate: evidence supports wafer-level packaging tools, but direct HBM/CoWoS/2.5D customer linkage is not yet proven and must be tested before promotion.

summary: Layer 1B expands the HBM/advanced-packaging equipment node with a bias toward US-listed, sub-$50B second-order suppliers. The highest-signal names in this pass are not HBM producers but vendors tied to inspection/metrology, probe cards, thermo-compression/hybrid bonding, and wafer-level packaging tools. Evidence strength is uneven: Camtek and FormFactor have explicit HBM-related product/order evidence; Kulicke & Soffa has explicit memory/HBM-adjacent advanced bonding evidence; ACM Research has advanced wafer-level packaging tool evidence but the direct HBM linkage remains a hypothesis to verify.
